generation.explanation: The matrix [[2, 1], [0, 1]] sends the basis vector î = (1, 0) to its first column, (2, 0), and sends ĵ = (0, 1) to its second column, (1, 1). That stretches the plane horizontally by 2 and shears it to the right. Grid lines stay parallel and evenly spaced. The yellow unit square becomes a parallelogram with corners (0,0), (2,0), (3,1) and (1,1). Its area is 2, and that equals the determinant: ad − bc = 2·1 − 1·0 = 2. The determinant is the factor by which the matrix scales every area. The shear (the 1 in the top right) slants the square without changing its area. The 2 doubles the width, and that is what doubles the area. Use the "Morph t" slider or the Animate button to watch the plane change gradually. You can also change a, b, c and d to try other matrices. When the determinant is 0, the plane flattens onto a line or a point. When it is negative, the square turns red because the plane has been flipped.
